@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KernelStartTimings:
    """Wall-clock timing breakdown for one kernel startup."""

    launch_seconds: float
    preamble_seconds: float
    total_seconds: float


class KernelExecutor:
    """
    Persistent sandboxed Python kernel for interactive data analysis.

    Usage::

        executor = KernelExecutor()
        await executor.start()          # boots kernel, runs preamble
        output = await executor.execute("df_train.describe()")
        await executor.stop()

    The kernel is started lazily by :meth:`execute` if :meth:`start` has not
    been called explicitly.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._km: AsyncKernelManager | None = None
        self._kc: AsyncKernelClient | None = None
        self._started: bool = False
        self._kernel_tmp_dir: str | None = None
        self._kernel_runtime_dir: str | None = None
        self._last_start_timings: KernelStartTimings | None = None
        # Session id of the launched kernel wrapper, used in stop() to reap any
        # apptainer exec / bwrap helpers that linger (see _reap_sandbox_session).
        self._sandbox_sid: int | None = None

    @property
    def is_started(self) -> bool:
        """True once the kernel process is up and the preamble has run."""
        return self._started

    @property
    def last_start_timings(self) -> KernelStartTimings | None:
        """Timing breakdown from the most recent :meth:`start` call."""
        return self._last_start_timings

    async def start(
        self,
        preamble: str | None = None,
        dataset_path: Path | None = None,
        kb_models_path: Path | None = None,
        kb_functions_path: Path | None = None,
        prebuilt_db_path: Path | None = None,
        prebuilt_db_dir: Path | None = None,
        kb_seeds_path: Path | None = None,
        thread_limit: int | None = None,
        kb_models_readonly: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """
        :param preamble: Optional Python code executed right after the kernel is
                         ready.  ``None`` by default — the kernel starts clean.
        :param thread_limit: When set, caps OpenMP/BLAS threads inside the kernel
                             (OMP_NUM_THREADS et al.) so concurrent pooled kernels
                             do not oversubscribe the CPU.  ``None`` leaves them
                             unset (backend default: one thread per core).
        :param dataset_path: When set, the dataset directory is bind-mounted
                             read-only into the sandbox (full file access).
                             When ``None``, the directory is excluded and
                             ``HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH`` is unset in the kernel env.
        :param kb_models_path: When set, the models directory is bind-mounted read-write into
                               the sandbox so the agent can persist trained ML model files there.
        :param kb_models_readonly: Bind the models directory read-only instead (sweep kernels:
                                   predict() only loads models, and anything it wrote there
                                   would be committed with the KB and seen by later sessions).
                                   Not enforced without a sandbox.
        :param kb_functions_path: When set, the functions directory is bind-mounted read-only
                                  into the sandbox so the agent can reload updated KB functions.
        :param prebuilt_db_path: When set, the parent directory of this pre-built patient DuckDB
                                 file is bind-mounted read-only.  Used by single-kernel sweep mode.
        :param prebuilt_db_dir: When set, this entire directory is bind-mounted read-only.
                                Used by pool mode.
        :param kb_seeds_path: When set, this directory is bind-mounted read-only as the seeds
                              directory so the synthesis agent can read all seed KBs.
        """
        _no_sandbox = os.environ.get("HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX", "0") not in ("", "0")

        if _no_sandbox:
            logger.info("Kernel sandbox: none (HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX)")
            sif_path: Path | None = None
        else:
            if shutil.which("apptainer") is None:
                raise KernelConfigError(
                    "Apptainer is required for kernel sandboxing but was not found on PATH.\n"
                    + "Run the setup script:\n"
                    + "  ./scripts/setup_sandbox.sh\n"
                    + "To skip isolation (development only): set HANCAS_NO_SANDBOX=1."
                )
            sif_path = _resolve_apptainer_sif()

        _sandboxed = sif_path is not None

        # Blocking filesystem calls below are run in a thread, not inline: this
        # coroutine can run on the same event loop as other concurrently-active
        # kernels (the sweep pool's background refill, in particular, starts a
        # replacement kernel while other kernels' predict()/cleanup calls are
        # still in flight on the same loop).  A synchronous mkdtemp/rmtree/write
        # that stalls on a contended host filesystem would otherwise freeze
        # message processing for every other kernel sharing the loop, making
        # them falsely appear unresponsive.
        # AF_UNIX socket paths are capped at 104-108 bytes depending on OS, so
        # this directory (holding only the tiny IPC connection file/sockets,
        # never large working data) needs to be short — macOS's default
        # TMPDIR (/var/folders/.../T/, ~40+ chars) alone leaves too little
        # room once the connection filename is appended. Pinned to bare /tmp
        # for that case. When sandboxed, tempfile.gettempdir() must be used
        # instead: _base_instance_binds() only bind-mounts that path (not
        # bare /tmp) into the Apptainer instance, and under Slurm it differs
        # from /tmp ($TMPDIR = /tmp/<jobid>, a sibling, not an ancestor) — a
        # hardcoded /tmp here would sit outside the instance's mounts, making
        # bwrap's bind of this dir fail with "Can't find source path" (the
        # cause of the tinyx job 1765161 failure). Linux $TMPDIR is always
        # short enough for the AF_UNIX limit, so this loses nothing there.
        _runtime_tmp_root = tempfile.gettempdir() if _sandboxed else "/tmp"
        self._kernel_runtime_dir = await asyncio.to_thread(
            tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix="hancas_kernel_runtime_", dir=_runtime_tmp_root
        )
        runtime_dir = Path(self._kernel_runtime_dir)
        _ = await asyncio.to_thread(_write_network_guard, runtime_dir)

        # Start (or reuse) the persistent Apptainer instance for this bind-set.
        instance_name: str | None = None
        connection_file_name: str = f"kernel-{uuid4()}.json"
        if _sandboxed:
            assert sif_path is not None
            # Install exit/SIGTERM cleanup here on the event-loop (main) thread —
            # the signal handler cannot be installed from the instance-start
            # worker thread below.
            _ensure_exit_cleanup_registered()
            # The KB working dirs are bound into the instance, so they must exist
            # before `apptainer instance start` (which fails on a missing mount
            # source).  The old per-kernel builder created these lazily; hoist it
            # here since the instance now starts first.  (The dataset and seeds
            # dirs must pre-exist and are not created.)
            def _mkdir_kb_dirs() -> None:
                for _kb_dir in (kb_models_path, kb_functions_path):
                    if _kb_dir is not None:
                        _kb_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

            await asyncio.to_thread(_mkdir_kb_dirs)
            data_binds = _instance_data_binds(
                dataset_path, kb_models_path, kb_functions_path, kb_seeds_path
            )
            handle = await asyncio.to_thread(
                _get_or_start_instance, sif_path, data_binds
            )
            instance_name = handle.name
            logger.info(
                "Kernel sandbox: instance %s + bwrap (%s)", instance_name, sif_path
            )

        km: AsyncKernelManager = AsyncKernelManager()

        # IPC transport over the private runtime dir, sandboxed or not: jupyter_client's
        # default TCP setup probes a free port, closes the probe socket, and hands the
        # bare port number to the newly-spawned kernel to bind later — a window where a
        # concurrently-starting kernel can grab the same port first. ipykernel's own
        # bind-retry logic (kernelapp.py's _bind_socket) only activates when the kernel
        # is free to pick its own port; since a specific number is always pinned here, a
        # collision is immediately fatal (zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use).
        # IPC sidesteps this with a private, guaranteed-unique named socket path instead
        # of a numbered port. For the sandboxed case, the runtime dir is bound at the
        # same real path inside bwrap, so one connection file works on both sides.
        km.transport = "ipc"
        km.connection_file = str(runtime_dir / connection_file_name)

        # jupyter_client 8.8+ builds the launch command from kernel_spec.argv.
        # Do NOT use km.kernel_cmd — that attribute is silently ignored in 8.8+,
        # which would start the kernel unsandboxed.
        kernel_spec = km.kernel_spec  # force-load the spec before mutation
        assert kernel_spec is not None
        kernel_spec.argv = _build_kernel_cmd(
            instance_name=instance_name,
            runtime_dir=runtime_dir if _sandboxed else None,
            connection_file_name=connection_file_name,
            dataset_path=dataset_path,
            kb_models_path=kb_models_path,
            kb_models_readonly=kb_models_readonly,
            kb_functions_path=kb_functions_path,
            kb_seeds_path=kb_seeds_path,
            prebuilt_db_path=prebuilt_db_path,
            prebuilt_db_dir=prebuilt_db_dir,
            use_net_isolation=_sandboxed and _max_net_namespaces() > 0,
            thread_limit=thread_limit,
        )

        if _sandboxed:
            # bwrap's --unshare-pid makes the tracked PID the wrapper, not the
            # kernel, so SIGINT (default "signal" mode) would never reach
            # ipykernel.  "message" sends interrupt_request on the ZMQ control
            # channel, which reaches ipykernel directly over the IPC socket.
            kernel_spec.interrupt_mode = "message"

        kernel_env: dict[str, str] | None = None
        if not _sandboxed:
            # Bare kernel (macOS or no sandbox): inherit host env but restrict
            # HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH and inject the Python-level network guard.
            self._kernel_tmp_dir = await asyncio.to_thread(
                tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix="hancas_kernel_"
            )
            kernel_env = {**os.environ, "TMPDIR": self._kernel_tmp_dir}
            if dataset_path is None:
                _ = kernel_env.pop("HANCOCK_DATASET_PATH", None)
            _existing_pp = kernel_env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
            kernel_env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
                f"{runtime_dir}:{_existing_pp}" if _existing_pp else str(runtime_dir)
            )
            if thread_limit is not None:
                for _thread_var in _THREAD_LIMIT_ENV_VARS:
                    kernel_env[_thread_var] = str(thread_limit)

        start_kwargs: dict[str, object] = {"stdout": subprocess.DEVNULL}
        if kernel_env is not None:
            start_kwargs["env"] = kernel_env

        start_t0 = time.monotonic()
        launch_t0 = time.monotonic()
        await km.start_kernel(**start_kwargs)  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]

        if _sandboxed:
            self._sandbox_sid = _read_sandbox_session_id(km)
            if self._sandbox_sid is not None:
                _active_sandbox_sids.add(self._sandbox_sid)

Owns everything about *running* the sandbox substrate, as opposed to building a
single kernel's launch command (see the ``sandbox_cmd`` module):

  * the persistent ``apptainer instance`` manager (one instance per config, keyed
    by data binds; started lazily, stopped at process exit) plus the startup
    sweep of orphaned instances leaked by hard-killed prior runs;
  * POSIX-session reaping of the per-kernel ``apptainer exec``/``bwrap`` subtree;
  * the atexit / SIGTERM cleanup registry and the lifecycle counters surfaced by
    ``kernel_process_report``.
"""

def _read_sandbox_session_id(km: "AsyncKernelManager") -> int | None:
    """
    Return the POSIX session id of the launched kernel-wrapper process.

    jupyter_client launches the kernel with ``start_new_session=True``, so the
    ``apptainer exec`` wrapper is a session leader (sid == pid).  Any helper
    processes it spawns stay in this session, so the session id is the reliable
    key for reaping the whole per-kernel subtree after shutdown.

    :param km: Kernel manager whose provisioner holds the launched pid.
    :return: Session id, or None if the pid is unknown or already gone.
    """
    provisioner = getattr(km, "provisioner", None)
    pid = getattr(provisioner, "pid", None)
    if not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0:
        return None
    try:
        return os.getsid(pid)
    except OSError:
        return None


def _session_pids(sid: int) -> list[int]:
    """
    PIDs currently in POSIX session *sid* (excluding the harness itself).

    Walks ``/proc``; used both to reap a kernel session and, afterwards, to
    verify that nothing survived the reap.  Never raises.

    :param sid: Session id captured at kernel start.
    :return: List of PIDs in the session, empty if none / on error.
    """
    if sid <= 0:
        return []
    self_pid = os.getpid()
    pids: list[int] = []
    try:
        entries = os.listdir("/proc")
    except OSError:
        return pids
    for entry in entries:
        if not entry.isdigit():
            continue
        pid = int(entry)
        if pid == self_pid:
            continue
        try:
            if os.getsid(pid) == sid:
                pids.append(pid)
        except OSError:
            continue
    return pids


def _reap_sandbox_session(sid: int) -> None:
    """
    Terminate any processes still alive in kernel session *sid*.

    ``shutdown_kernel`` kills only the kernel's process group; the
    ``apptainer exec``/``bwrap`` wrappers may linger in the session.  They remain
    in the kernel's session, so reaping by session id removes exactly the
    per-kernel subtree and nothing else (never the persistent Apptainer
    instance, which runs in its own session).

    Best-effort: SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL for any straggler.

    :param sid: Session id captured at kernel start.
    """
    if sid <= 0:
        return

    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
        pids = _session_pids(sid)
        if not pids:
            return
        for pid in pids:
            try:
                os.kill(pid, sig)
            except OSError:
                continue
        time.sleep(0.2)

class Deps:

async def goto(ctx: RunContext[Deps], url: str) -> str:
    """Open a URL or a path on this website (e.g. a link's target from the page)."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    await session.revive()
    target = urljoin(session.page.url, url)
    if urlparse(target).netloc != urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc:
        return f"{target} is not on this website ({session.site['url']}); stay on it."
    async with session.lock:
        await session._goto(target)
        session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="goto", url=target)
        return await session.look(brief=True)


async def click(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str) -> str:
    """Click the element with this ref (link, button, tab, summary, checkbox)."""
    return await ctx.deps.session.act("click", ref, _click)


async def fill(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, text: str, submit: bool = False) -> str:
    """Type text into a textbox or textarea (replaces its content), or set a slider to a number.

    submit=true presses Enter afterwards, which runs a search or sends the field's form.
    """
    async def run(element):
        if await element.evaluate("e => e.type") == "range":
            await element.evaluate("(e, v) => { e.value = v; e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true}));"
                                   " e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); }", text)
        else:
            await element.fill(text, timeout=5000)
        if submit:
            await element.press("Enter")
    return await ctx.deps.session.act("fill", ref, run)


LABELS_JS = r"""
e => Array.from(e.options || []).map(o =>
  [o.textContent.replace(/[\u200b\u200c\u200d\u2060\ufeff\u00ad]/g, '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(), o.value])

def _option_index(choices: list[list[str]], option: str) -> int | None:
    """The option whose visible text (else value) is `option`, ignoring spacing and then case."""
    want = " ".join(option.split())
    for match in (lambda t, v: t == want, lambda t, v: v == option, lambda t, v: t.casefold() == want.casefold()):
        for i, (text, value) in enumerate(choices):
            if match(text, value):
                return i
    return None


def _close_options(texts: list[str], option: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[str]:
    """Options that contain `option`, else any of its words, for a helpful error."""
    want = option.casefold().strip()
    hits = [t for t in texts if want and want in t.casefold()]
    if not hits:
        words = [w for w in want.replace(",", " ").split() if len(w) > 1]
        hits = [t for t in texts if any(w in t.casefold() for w in words)]
    return hits[:limit]


async def select(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, option: str) -> str:
    """Choose an option of a select by its visible text."""
    async def run(element):
        choices = await element.evaluate(LABELS_JS)
        index = _option_index(choices, option)
        if index is None:
            texts = [text for text, _ in choices]
            close = _close_options(texts, option)
            hint = f"options like it: {' | '.join(close)}" if close else f"options({ref}, contains) searches them"
            raise ValueError(f"no option {option!r} among {len(texts)}; {hint}")
        await element.select_option(index=index, timeout=5000)
    return await ctx.deps.session.act("select", ref, run)


async def options(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, contains: str = "") -> str:
    """List the options of a select (views shorten long lists), or only those whose text contains `contains`."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    async with session.lock:
        found = await select_options(session.page, ref, contains)
    if found is None:
        return f"No select {ref} on this page (refs change with every view)."
    total, hits = found
    which = f" containing {contains!r}" if contains else ""
    text = f"{len(hits)} of {total} options of {ref}{which}:\n" + "\n".join(hits[:300])
    if len(hits) > 300:
        text += f"\n... {len(hits) - 300} more; narrow with contains"
    session.seen += "\n" + text
    return text


async def check(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, checked: bool = True) -> str:
    """Tick (checked=true) or untick a checkbox or radio button."""
    async def run(element):

        except Exception:
            await element.evaluate("(e, c) => { if (e.checked !== c) e.click(); }", checked)
    return await ctx.deps.session.act("check", ref, run)


async def back(ctx: RunContext[Deps], reason: str = "") -> str:

# A run of value characters; those with a digit are values. (The former single pattern, [..]*\d[..]*, retried
# every start of a long run without a digit: quadratic, minutes on one long token.)
VALUE_RUN = re.compile(r"[\w/.:,+-]+")
DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def unseen_values(text: str, seen: str) -> list[str]:
    """The values in `text` (anything with a digit: numbers, references, dates) that `seen` does not contain."""
    missing = []  # a value holds no whitespace, so searching `seen` as is matches its whitespace-normalised form
    for token in VALUE_RUN.findall(text):
        if not DIGIT.search(token):
            continue
        token = token.strip(".,:;/-+")
        if token and token not in seen and token not in missing:
            missing.append(token)
    return missing


async def note(ctx: RunContext[Deps], key: str, value: str) -> str:
    """Record a fact you can see on the current page (copy values exactly), so it survives if you run out of time."""
    missing = unseen_values(value, ctx.deps.session.seen)
    if missing:
        ctx.deps.session.trace.event(ctx.deps.session.name, "note_refused", key=key, missing=missing[:10])
        ctx.deps.refused[key] = ctx.deps.refused.get(key, 0) + 1
        if ctx.deps.refused[key] > 2:
            return (f"Not noted, again. Stop trying to note {key!r}; continue with your goal from what the current "
                    f"page shows.")
        return (f"Not noted: {', '.join(missing[:10])} appear on no page you have seen. Note only values copied "
                f"from a page; open the page again if you need to check.")
    ctx.deps.notes[key] = value
    ctx.deps.session.trace.event(ctx.deps.session.name, "note", key=key, value=value)
    return f"noted {key}"

        it closes, or when its page stops answering (STUCK_SECONDS). Failed attempts are retried in a fresh

    """
    Persistent sandboxed Python kernel for interactive data analysis.

    Usage::

        executor = KernelExecutor()
        await executor.start()          # boots kernel, runs preamble

        await executor.stop()

    been called explicitly.

        self._km: AsyncKernelManager | None = None
        self._kc: AsyncKernelClient | None = None
        self._started: bool = False
        self._kernel_tmp_dir: str | None = None
        self._kernel_runtime_dir: str | None = None
        self._last_start_timings: KernelStartTimings | None = None
        # Session id of the launched kernel wrapper, used in stop() to reap any
        # apptainer exec / bwrap helpers that linger (see _reap_sandbox_session).
        self._sandbox_sid: int | None = None

    @property
    def is_started(self) -> bool:
        """True once the kernel process is up and the preamble has run."""
        return self._started

    @property
    def last_start_timings(self) -> KernelStartTimings | None:
        """Timing breakdown from the most recent :meth:`start` call."""

        :param thread_limit: When set, caps OpenMP/BLAS threads inside the kernel

                             do not oversubscribe the CPU.  ``None`` leaves them

        :param dataset_path: When set, the dataset directory is bind-mounted
                             read-only into the sandbox (full file access).

        :param kb_models_path: When set, the models directory is bind-mounted read-write into

        :param kb_models_readonly: Bind the models directory read-only instead (sweep kernels:

def _read_sandbox_session_id(km: "AsyncKernelManager") -> int | None:
    """
    Return the POSIX session id of the launched kernel-wrapper process.

    jupyter_client launches the kernel with ``start_new_session=True``, so the
    ``apptainer exec`` wrapper is a session leader (sid == pid).  Any helper
    processes it spawns stay in this session, so the session id is the reliable
    key for reaping the whole per-kernel subtree after shutdown.

    :param km: Kernel manager whose provisioner holds the launched pid.
    :return: Session id, or None if the pid is unknown or already gone.
    """
    provisioner = getattr(km, "provisioner", None)
    pid = getattr(provisioner, "pid", None)
    if not isinstance(pid, int) or pid <= 0:
        return None
    try:
        return os.getsid(pid)
    except OSError:
        return None


def _session_pids(sid: int) -> list[int]:
    """
    PIDs currently in POSIX session *sid* (excluding the harness itself).

    Walks ``/proc``; used both to reap a kernel session and, afterwards, to
    verify that nothing survived the reap.  Never raises.

    :param sid: Session id captured at kernel start.
    :return: List of PIDs in the session, empty if none / on error.
    """
    if sid <= 0:
        return []
    self_pid = os.getpid()
    pids: list[int] = []
    try:
        entries = os.listdir("/proc")
    except OSError:
        return pids
    for entry in entries:
        if not entry.isdigit():
            continue
        pid = int(entry)
        if pid == self_pid:
            continue
        try:
            if os.getsid(pid) == sid:
                pids.append(pid)
        except OSError:
            continue
    return pids


def _reap_sandbox_session(sid: int) -> None:
    """
    Terminate any processes still alive in kernel session *sid*.

    ``shutdown_kernel`` kills only the kernel's process group; the
    ``apptainer exec``/``bwrap`` wrappers may linger in the session.  They remain
    in the kernel's session, so reaping by session id removes exactly the
    per-kernel subtree and nothing else (never the persistent Apptainer
    instance, which runs in its own session).

    Best-effort: SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL for any straggler.

    :param sid: Session id captured at kernel start.
    """
    if sid <= 0:
        return

    for sig in (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGKILL):
        pids = _session_pids(sid)
        if not pids:
            return
        for pid in pids:
            try:
                os.kill(pid, sig)
            except OSError:
                continue
        time.sleep(0.2)

async def goto(ctx: RunContext[Deps], url: str) -> str:
    """Open a URL or a path on this website (e.g. a link's target from the page)."""
    session = ctx.deps.session
    await session.revive()
    target = urljoin(session.page.url, url)
    if urlparse(target).netloc != urlparse(session.site["url"]).netloc:
        return f"{target} is not on this website ({session.site['url']}); stay on it."
    async with session.lock:
        await session._goto(target)
        session.trace.event(session.name, "action", action="goto", url=target)
        return await session.look(brief=True)

def _option_index(choices: list[list[str]], option: str) -> int | None:
    """The option whose visible text (else value) is `option`, ignoring spacing and then case."""
    want = " ".join(option.split())
    for match in (lambda t, v: t == want, lambda t, v: v == option, lambda t, v: t.casefold() == want.casefold()):
        for i, (text, value) in enumerate(choices):
            if match(text, value):
                return i
    return None


def _close_options(texts: list[str], option: str, limit: int = 8) -> list[str]:
    """Options that contain `option`, else any of its words, for a helpful error."""
    want = option.casefold().strip()
    hits = [t for t in texts if want and want in t.casefold()]
    if not hits:
        words = [w for w in want.replace(",", " ").split() if len(w) > 1]
        hits = [t for t in texts if any(w in t.casefold() for w in words)]
    return hits[:limit]


async def select(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, option: str) -> str:
    """Choose an option of a select by its visible text."""
    async def run(element):
        choices = await element.evaluate(LABELS_JS)
        index = _option_index(choices, option)
        if index is None:
            texts = [text for text, _ in choices]
            close = _close_options(texts, option)
            hint = f"options like it: {' | '.join(close)}" if close else f"options({ref}, contains) searches them"
            raise ValueError(f"no option {option!r} among {len(texts)}; {hint}")
        await element.select_option(index=index, timeout=5000)
    return await ctx.deps.session.act("select", ref, run)

    async with session.lock:
        found = await select_options(session.page, ref, contains)
    if found is None:
        return f"No select {ref} on this page (refs change with every view)."
    total, hits = found
    which = f" containing {contains!r}" if contains else ""
    text = f"{len(hits)} of {total} options of {ref}{which}:\n" + "\n".join(hits[:300])

# A run of value characters; those with a digit are values. (The former single pattern, [..]*\d[..]*, retried
# every start of a long run without a digit: quadratic, minutes on one long token.)
VALUE_RUN = re.compile(r"[\w/.:,+-]+")
DIGIT = re.compile(r"\d")


def unseen_values(text: str, seen: str) -> list[str]:
    """The values in `text` (anything with a digit: numbers, references, dates) that `seen` does not contain."""
    missing = []  # a value holds no whitespace, so searching `seen` as is matches its whitespace-normalised form
    for token in VALUE_RUN.findall(text):
        if not DIGIT.search(token):
            continue
        token = token.strip(".,:;/-+")
        if token and token not in seen and token not in missing:
            missing.append(token)
    return missing


async def note(ctx: RunContext[Deps], key: str, value: str) -> str:
    """Record a fact you can see on the current page (copy values exactly), so it survives if you run out of time."""
    missing = unseen_values(value, ctx.deps.session.seen)
    if missing:
        ctx.deps.session.trace.event(ctx.deps.session.name, "note_refused", key=key, missing=missing[:10])
        ctx.deps.refused[key] = ctx.deps.refused.get(key, 0) + 1
        if ctx.deps.refused[key] > 2:
            return (f"Not noted, again. Stop trying to note {key!r}; continue with your goal from what the current "
                    f"page shows.")

"""
The agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

v2: read the brief, then the orchestrator (planner, findings board, research workers, verifier, calc) builds the
answer, and submit.py enters and signs the bid with it; without an answer every position is omitted, as in v1.
AGENT_RESEARCH=0 skips the research (the v1 path). See docs/plan.md.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import localenv  # noqa: F401  (first: local runs read agent/.env before any module reads its settings)
import browser_tools
import browsers
import loopwatch
import run as contract
from briefing import read_brief
from browser_tools import SiteSession
from orchestrator import Orchestrator
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright
from submit import BidFlow, Mailbox, submit_bid
import tracing
from tracing import Trace

SAFETY_SECONDS = 90  # the answer must be in before the run expires
LOCAL_SECONDS = 20 * 60  # the scouting run does not expire; behave like a scored run
RESEARCH_START_SECONDS = 600  # a website that only research needs is warmed this long, then given up


def warm_up(sessions: dict[str, SiteSession], deadline: float, critical: set[str]) -> dict[str, asyncio.Task]:
    """
    Start signing in to every website in the background and return at once: nothing waits for all of them. The
    `critical` ones (the bid website, the mailbox) keep retrying until START_MARGIN before the deadline; the others
    give up after RESEARCH_START_SECONDS. A session whose start is still running can be handed out: its first look
    waits for the start (SiteSession.revive).
    """
    browser_tools.DEADLINE = deadline
    tasks = {}
    for name, session in sessions.items():
        limit = deadline - browser_tools.START_MARGIN
        if name not in critical:
            limit = min(limit, time.monotonic() + RESEARCH_START_SECONDS)
        session.until = limit
        tasks[name] = asyncio.create_task(session.start(until=limit), name=f"start@{name}")
        tasks[name].add_done_callback(lambda t: t.cancelled() or t.exception())  # failures are traced in start
    return tasks


async def solve(task: dict, page, answer: dict | None = None,
                attributes: dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None = None) -> dict | None:
    """
    Enter the bid on the run's website (a "site" submission) and return None.

    `answer` (calc's BidResult.answer()) and `attributes` (per position, the chosen material's attributes) are what
    the bid worker enters; positions they do not give completely are omitted. Unless given, the orchestrator
    researches them; a research failure never costs the signed bid.
    """
    trace = Trace()
    loopwatch.Watchdog(activity=lambda: trace.last).start()  # a blocked loop or a silent run dumps its stacks
    left = min(contract.seconds_left(task), LOCAL_SECONDS)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + left - SAFETY_SECONDS
    # Sign in to every website in the background: the brief, the planner and the workers never wait for all of
    # them. The bid website (named by the run contract) keeps warming; the mailbox too, once the brief names it.
    contexts = await browsers.more_contexts(page, len(task["access"]))
    sessions = {site["siteId"]: SiteSession(site, context, trace) for site, context in zip(task["access"], contexts)}
    contract_site = (task.get("submission") or {}).get("siteId")
    starts = warm_up(sessions, deadline, {contract_site} if contract_site in sessions else set(sessions))
    briefing = await read_brief(task)
    # The run contract names the submission website; it wins over the model's reading of the brief.
    if contract_site in sessions and contract_site != briefing.bid_site:
        trace.event("briefing", "bid_site_corrected", read=briefing.bid_site, contract=contract_site)
        briefing = briefing.model_copy(update={"bid_site": contract_site})
    trace.event("briefing", "done", **briefing.model_dump(exclude={"submission_steps"}))
    bid, mail = sessions[briefing.bid_site], sessions[briefing.mail_site]
    for session in (bid, mail):  # critical after all: warm until the margin before the deadline
        session.until = max(session.until or 0, deadline - browser_tools.START_MARGIN)
    # The bid form's steps that need no research (bidder data, offer type) run while the research does.
    flow = BidFlow(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline)
    flow.start()
    if answer is None and os.environ.get("AGENT_RESEARCH", "1") != "0":
        answer, attributes = await research(task, briefing, contexts, trace, deadline, sessions)
    # A start still running is waited for by the session's first look; one that gave up gets a fresh tab there.
    trace.event("starts", "state", **{name: ("up" if s.ok else "starting" if s.starting else "down")
                                      for name, s in sessions.items()}, pending=sum(not t.done() for t in starts.values()))
    try:
        result = await flow.finish(answer, attributes)
    except Exception as error:  # never end without trying to sign: one more pass with what is on screen
        trace.event("submit", "crashed", error=f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
        result = await submit_bid(bid, Mailbox(mail, briefing, deadline), briefing, deadline, answer, attributes)
    trace.event("result", "done", result=result.model_dump() if result else None)
    return None


async def research(task: dict, briefing, contexts: list, trace: Trace, deadline: float,
                   warm: dict[str, SiteSession] | None = None) -> tuple[dict | None, dict[str, dict[str, str]] | None]:
    """The orchestrator's answer and material attributes; (None, None) when it fails or builds nothing."""
    answer, attributes, problems = None, None, []
    orchestrator = None
    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        orchestrator = Orchestrator(task, briefing, {s["siteId"]: c for s, c in zip(task["access"], contexts)},
                                    trace, deadline, warm=warm)

*** Add File: /private/tmp/ehl-kernel-prototype/agent/code_kernel.py
+"""Optional model-directed analysis of a selected, inert page snapshot.
+
+The workspace uses a separate context in an already supplied browser. It has no
+site cookies, is offline, and never receives a live Page or Playwright handle.
+It persists JavaScript `state` across a worker's cells; each cell receives a
+fresh DOMParser document for the element the model selected.
+"""
+import asyncio
+import os
+
+from extract import locate
+from pydantic_ai import RunContext
+
+from browser_tools import Deps
+
+MAX_SNAPSHOT = 250_000
+MAX_OUTPUT = 4_000
+CELL_SECONDS = 3
+
+SNAPSHOT_JS = r"""
+el => {
+  const root = el.cloneNode(true);
+  const original = [el, ...el.querySelectorAll('*')];
+  const copies = [root, ...root.querySelectorAll('*')];
+  const blocked = new Set(['SCRIPT', 'STYLE', 'NOSCRIPT', 'TEMPLATE', 'META', 'LINK']);
+  for (let i = 0; i < original.length; i++) {
+    const src = original[i], dst = copies[i];
+    if (blocked.has(src.tagName) || src.hidden || src.inert ||
+        src.getAttribute('aria-hidden') === 'true' ||
+        (src.tagName === 'INPUT' && src.type === 'password') ||
+        getComputedStyle(src).display === 'none' ||
+        getComputedStyle(src).visibility === 'hidden') {
+      dst.remove();
+      continue;
+    }
+    for (const attr of [...dst.attributes]) {
+      if (/^on/i.test(attr.name) || ['src', 'srcset', 'style'].includes(attr.name))
+        dst.removeAttribute(attr.name);
+    }
+    if (src.tagName === 'INPUT' && src.type !== 'password') dst.setAttribute('value', src.value);
+    if (src.tagName === 'TEXTAREA') dst.textContent = src.value;
+  }
+  return {html: root.outerHTML, text: root.textContent || ''};
+}
+"""
+
+CELL_JS = r"""
+async ({html, code}) => {
+  const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, 'text/html');
+  const lines = [];
+  const write = (...items) => lines.push(items.map(x =>
+    typeof x === 'string' ? x : JSON.stringify(x)).join(' '));
+  const output = {log: write, error: write, warn: write};
+  try {
+    const fn = new (async function(){}).constructor('doc', 'state', 'console', code);
+    const result = await fn(doc, window.__codeState, output);
+    if (result !== undefined) write(result);
+  } catch (error) {
+    write(`${error.name}: ${error.message}`);
+  }
+  return lines.join('\n');
+}
+"""
+
+
+class CodeKernel:
+    def __init__(self, browser):
+        self.browser = browser
+        self.context = None
+        self.page = None
+        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
+
+    async def execute(self, html: str, code: str) -> str:
+        async with self.lock:
+            if self.page is None:
+                self.context = await self.browser.new_context(offline=True)
+                await self.context.route('**/*', lambda route: route.abort())
+                self.page = await self.context.new_page()
+                await self.page.goto('about:blank')
+                await self.page.evaluate('window.__codeState = {}')
+            try:
+                result = await asyncio.wait_for(
+                    self.page.evaluate(CELL_JS, {'html': html, 'code': code}), CELL_SECONDS)
+            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+                await self.close()
+                return f'Code cell exceeded {CELL_SECONDS} seconds; workspace reset.'
+            return result[:MAX_OUTPUT] + ('\n[output truncated]' if len(result) > MAX_OUTPUT else '')
+
+    async def close(self):
+        if self.context is not None:
+            await self.context.close()
+        self.context = self.page = None
+
+
+async def analyze_selected(ctx: RunContext[Deps], ref: str, code: str) -> str:
+    """Run JavaScript on one model-selected page element; use ref='page' for the current page.
+
+    In code, query the inert `doc` with DOM methods, use `state` to keep data for
+    later cells, and `console.log(...)` or `return ...` for a short answer.
+    This tool cannot click, navigate or inspect a different website.
+    """
+    session = ctx.deps.session
+    async with session.lock:
+        await session.revive()
+        element = session.page.locator('body') if ref == 'page' else await locate(session.page, ref)
+        if element is None:
+            return f'No element {ref} on this page; choose a ref from the current view.'
+        snapshot = await element.evaluate(SNAPSHOT_JS)
+    html = snapshot['html']
+    if len(html) > MAX_SNAPSHOT:
+        return f'Selected element is {len(html)} characters; choose a smaller ref.'
+    session.seen += '\n' + snapshot['text']
+    kernel = ctx.deps.code_kernel
+    result = await kernel.execute(html, code)
+    session.trace.event(session.name, 'code_cell', ref=ref, snapshot_chars=len(html),
+                        code_chars=len(code), output_chars=len(result))
+    return result or '(no output; use console.log or return)'
+
+
+def enabled() -> bool:
+    return os.environ.get('AGENT_CODE_KERNEL') == '1'
*** End Patch";

*** Add File: /private/tmp/ehl-kernel-prototype/docs/code-kernel-prototype.md
+# Model-directed code workspace prototype
+
+Set `AGENT_CODE_KERNEL=1` to give each browser worker an optional `analyze_selected(ref, code)` tool. The model still chooses the page, record, search and element. The tool copies that one selected visible DOM subtree into an inert document and runs its JavaScript against it. `state` persists across cells in the worker, so the model can keep a compact derived table and query it again without sending the full page through its prompt. Every worker gets its own context; it closes when the worker ends. Default is off.
+
+Example on an invented register (the model supplies this code):
+
+```javascript
+state.rows = [...doc.querySelectorAll('tr')].map(row =>
+  [...row.cells].map(cell => cell.textContent.trim()));
+return state.rows.filter(row => row[1] === '40 mm').map(row => row[0]);
+```
+
+This uses an extra context of an **existing provided browser**, never a new browser process. The context is offline, blocks HTTP requests and WebSockets, and has no site cookies or opener. It receives inert HTML with scripts, handlers, external resources, password inputs and hidden elements removed. It cannot act on the live site through the tool. Cell time, code length, output length and number of cells are bounded. A selected snapshot's visible text is added to the worker's grounding record.
+
+This is a scoped browser JavaScript workspace, not an OS security boundary. Hancas's Python `KernelExecutor` relies on Apptainer and bubblewrap isolation; copying its bare Python fallback into this challenge package would let model-authored code read process secrets and files. A Python kernel is possible only with a verified sandbox substrate in the challenge environment. The current prototype also does not inspect cross-origin frames through a parent page snapshot; choose a ref in the frame, which `locate` can resolve.
+
+## Synthetic microbenchmark
+
+Run `cd agent && uv run --no-sync python ../dev/code_kernel_bench.py`. The fixture is an invented 600-row register. On one local run:
+
+| Method | Model-visible characters | `chars / 4` token proxy | Local browser time |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Existing `observe` + `read_more` | 37,219 in 3 chunks | 9,305 | 10.3 ms to observe |
+| Existing `collect` | 13,001; first 200 rows | 3,251 | 28.1 ms |
+| One code cell + result | 381 | 96 | 21.6 ms snapshot + 36.0 ms cold / 2.5 ms warm cell |
+
+The token proxy is **not measured model tokens**. The code cell has to be written by the model and the current worker already has an initial page view, so these figures do not imply a 97% run-level saving. # Model-directed code workspace prototype

Set `AGENT_CODE_KERNEL=1` to give each browser worker an optional `analyze_selected(ref, code)` tool. The model still chooses the page, record, search and element. The tool copies that one selected visible DOM subtree into an inert document and runs its JavaScript against it. `state` persists across cells in the worker, so the model can keep a compact derived table and query it again without sending the full page through its prompt. Every worker gets its own context; it closes when the worker ends. Default is off.

Example on an invented register (the model supplies this code):

```javascript
state.rows = [...doc.querySelectorAll('tr')].map(row =>
  [...row.cells].map(cell => cell.textContent.trim()));
return state.rows.filter(row => row[1] === '40 mm').map(row => row[0]);
```

This uses an extra context of an **existing provided browser**, never a new browser process. The context is offline, blocks HTTP requests and WebSockets, and has no site cookies or opener. It receives inert HTML with scripts, handlers, external resources, password inputs and hidden elements removed. It cannot act on the live site through the tool. Cell time, code length, output length and number of cells are bounded. A selected snapshot's visible text is added to the worker's grounding record.

This is a scoped browser JavaScript workspace, not an OS security boundary. Hancas's Python `KernelExecutor` relies on Apptainer and bubblewrap isolation; copying its bare Python fallback into this challenge package would let model-authored code read process secrets and files. A Python kernel is possible only with a verified sandbox substrate in the challenge environment. The current prototype also does not inspect cross-origin frames through a parent page snapshot; choose a ref in the frame, which `locate` can resolve.

## Synthetic microbenchmark

Run `cd agent && uv run --no-sync python ../dev/code_kernel_bench.py`. The fixture is an invented 600-row register. On one local run:

| Method | Model-visible characters | `chars / 4` token proxy | Local browser time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Existing `observe` + `read_more` | 37,219 in 3 chunks | 9,305 | 10.3 ms to observe |
| Existing `collect` | 13,001; first 200 rows | 3,251 | 28.1 ms |
| One code cell + result | 381 | 96 | 21.6 ms snapshot + 36.0 ms cold / 2.5 ms warm cell |

The token proxy is **not measured model tokens**. The code cell has to be written by the model and the current worker already has an initial page view, so these figures do not imply a 97% run-level saving. They show the opportunity when a model needs a narrow answer from a dense selected page. No Qwen A/B or public challenge run has tested quality, actual tokens or end-to-end time. The local proxy was inaccessible from this worktree's execution environment. Before enabling by default, run a synthetic Qwen A/B and a public test run, then compare quality and whole-run token/call/time records.

The main risk is extra model effort: writing code can cost more turns than `collect` on short lists, and arbitrary code can return a plausible but wrong filter. Keep it optional for dense pages and verify decisive facts against the selected evidence.
